clue.text: Resign as side loses heart in cup

parts.note: to demit is an old word meaning to resign an office

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letters of the word side are dropped, leaving its ends

parts.note: taken as written before its middle goes

explanation.surface: A team member quits as the team, demoralised, crashes out of a cup competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cup' looks like a trophy, but it is the small coffee cup. 'loses heart' drops ID from SIDE, leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small coffee cup, the French name meaning half a cup.

clue.text: I am Richard, almost a professional

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm, and the speaker is me

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the name is left off

parts.note: Dick is a familiar form of the name Richard

explanation.surface: Someone called Richard boasts of being nearly a qualified professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the K from DICK, leaving DIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A medic is a doctor, a member of the medical profession, so a professional.

clue.text: Pronounced letters badly? Relax!

definitions.meaning: the letters S and F, properly said ess and eff, said poorly might come out as ease and off
an order to slacken off or take things easier

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is playful: mispronounce the names of the letters S and F and you get the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to slacken or let up, an idiom for relaxing.

clue.text: Patchy condition of fast travel limiting one

indicators.note: the pair of words limit, or hem in, the numeral, so it sits between them

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
to go is to travel
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A doctor describes a skin condition caught on a fast trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentigo is a medical term for a small brown patch on the skin, a freckle or age spot.

clue.text: German author, a gift from heaven

parts.note: Thomas Mann was a German novelist, author of The Magic Mountain

explanation.surface: A great German novelist is hailed as a divine blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Exodus manna was food sent down from heaven to the Israelites, so figuratively any windfall.

clue.text: Danger at sea daily repelled by detectives

parts.note: a daily is a British term for a cleaning lady, also called a char

indicators.note: repelled means the little word by is turned back

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman fends off police officers in a threatening situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' turns BY into YB. 'daily' is a noun here, the British cleaning lady, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Charybdis was the whirlpool of Greek myth facing Scylla, a peril for sailors.

clue.text: Military team in brief not forthcoming

definitions.meaning: The military abbreviation of company, a unit of soldiers
reticent, shy, unwilling to reveal things

explanation.definitionFit: Being coy means pretending to be shy and holding back, so not forthcoming.

clue.text: Plant produces new tree ring irregularly

indicators.note: irregularly means the letters are set out in no fixed order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plant puts out new growth rings unevenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produces' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintergreen is an evergreen shrub whose leaves give a minty oil.

clue.text: Bring in one making endless requests

parts.note: to import is to bring goods in from abroad
unity is the state of being one

explanation.surface: Someone tries to bring in a colleague who keeps nagging.
explanation.definitionFit: Importunity is persistent pestering with demands, so the act of making endless requests.

clue.text: Plead, being fat, to lose a little

indicators.note: losing a little means a small part, the last letter, is shed

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat used in cooking

explanation.surface: A dieter begs to shed some weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' and 'to' are link words; 'lose a little' drops the T from SUET.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to plead or appeal, as in suing for peace.

clue.text: Spirit not for mixing?

parts.note: fire and water famously do not mix, yet joined as one word they name a strong liquor, which you might drink neat

explanation.definitionFit: Firewater is a jocular name for strong alcoholic spirits such as whisky.

clue.text: Sort of clock in marine style?

parts.note: with style, in a given style is the French a la
RM is the abbreviation for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: Is this timepiece made in a naval fashion?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... style' is the French à la, as in à la mode.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm clock is one that rings to wake you, so alarm describes a kind of clock.

clue.text: Poet's hurrying as battle not finished

indicators.note: not finished means the last letter of the battle's name is lopped off

parts.note: the Battle of Hastings in 1066 is England's most famous battle

explanation.surface: A poet rushes into verse about an unfinished battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To haste is an old, poetic verb for to hurry, so its present participle means hurrying.

clue.text: Thanks college for what one has earned

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
King's is a college at Cambridge (and in London)

explanation.surface: A grateful student thanks the college for their wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are money received, as a shop's daily earnings.

clue.text: One may be taken by doctor back up at college

definitions.text: One may be taken by doctor

indicators.note: back means the little word up is read in reverse

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A doctor at college returns to take a measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word; 'back' turns UP into PU.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor takes your pulse, counting heartbeats at the wrist.

clue.text: Sun-dried grape finally rotted, not for picking

indicators.note: rotted fruit has broken down, so the letters are broken up into a new order
finally means only the last letter of grape is used

explanation.surface: A sun-dried grape has gone bad and is not worth harvesting.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange SUNDRIED plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undesired is unwanted, so nobody would choose it.

clue.text: Imagine energy-filled drink

indicators.note: filled with energy means the physics symbol goes inside the drink

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of whisky
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Picture an energy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream of something is to imagine or fantasise about it.

clue.text: Craft boy runs in springtime

indicators.note: in places the boy and runs inside the spring month

parts.note: May is a month of spring
a son is a boy
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A boy races about in spring in his little boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry is the craft or trade of a stonemason, building with stone.

clue.text: Ten-year struggle against computer hackers?

definitions.meaning: the siege of Troy by the Greeks lasted ten years
a Trojan is malicious software that sneaks into a computer, so a war on such programs could take this name

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is playful: a campaign fighting Trojan horse viruses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan War was the legendary decade-long conflict between Greeks and Troy.

clue.text: Pass, wearing seatbelt for example

definitions.meaning: a document that guarantees a traveller passage through hostile territory
read literally, careful and secure behaviour behind the wheel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' is a noun, a permit for travel, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe conduct is official protection or a permit granting secure passage.

clue.text: Slipper, or (commonly) part of one

indicators.note: commonly means said in a common, Cockney way, dropping the initial aitch

parts.note: the heel is part of a slipper, the shoe

explanation.surface: Something slippery, or a bit of a bedroom shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slipper' is a slippery creature here, not footwear, though 'part of one' then takes the footwear sense. 'or' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a slippery fish, so jokingly a slipper, one that slips away.

clue.text: In my case, a single change

indicators.note: case means the word my forms a casing round the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
a single is one

explanation.surface: Someone notes that, for them, one small adjustment will do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link word. 'change' is the noun for coins, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Change is loose coins, a form of money.

clue.text: Get less trickery, having daughter instead of son

indicators.note: instead of means one letter replaces the other in the word for trickery

parts.note: a swindle is a fraud, a piece of trickery
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A family scam shrinks when the daughter replaces the son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to diminish gradually, to become smaller in amount.

clue.text: Decorative technique one's working into identical copy

indicators.note: into means the first pieces go inside the copy

parts.note: a clone is an identical copy
one's is I'S, I for one plus S
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Someone's craft method is putting effort into exact replicas.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloisonné is an enamelling technique using cells formed by thin metal strips.

clue.text: Got better value finally — new tailor-made clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here, the rearranged letters dressing round the final letter
new means the letters of tailor-made are made over in a fresh order
finally means only the last letter of value is used

explanation.surface: Someone's worth rose at last thanks to new bespoke clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns TAILORMADE into AMELIORATD, which 'clothes' wraps round E.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to improve or make better; ameliorated can mean improved.

clue.text: Check wife wiggling part of body for politician

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

indicators.note: wiggling means the letters of wife are wriggled round

parts.note: the hip is a part of the body

explanation.surface: Someone checks their wife's dancing hip, of all things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief whip is the senior party official keeping MPs in line in British politics.

clue.text: Chap pretends to embrace wife's effigy

parts.note: a guy is a chap

indicators.note: to embrace means the word for pretends hugs the letter inside it

parts.note: fakes means pretends
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A man feigns affection to cuddle his wife's statue.
explanation.walkthrough: A Guy Fawkes is the dummy burned on Bonfire Night, 5 November, in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: On Bonfire Night a stuffed figure of the Gunpowder plotter is burned, so an effigy.

clue.text: Like to enter short promise to behave — it takes the heat off

indicators.note: to enter means the first word goes inside the cut-down promise
short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: parole is a prisoner's promise of good conduct
as means like

explanation.surface: A prisoner's pledge, briefly, lets them escape the pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims PAROLE to PAROL, which AS enters.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a sunshade, which keeps the heat of the sun off you.

clue.text: Tool, small, I got out of bag

indicators.note: got out of means the single letter is removed from the bag

parts.note: a pannier is a bag on a bicycle or a pack animal

explanation.surface: A small tool I took out of my bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got out of' removes I from PANNIER, leaving PANNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A spanner is a tool for turning nuts and bolts, called a wrench in the US.

clue.text: Unattractive complaint: husband's red perhaps all over

indicators.note: all over means the wine is spread around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: red is an example of wine
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife grumbles that her husband has spilt red wine everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks red as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A whine is a querulous, grating complaint, unpleasant to hear.

clue.text: Millions applied thought

parts.note: applied means used, as with a tool

explanation.surface: Millions were spent after careful thought.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder, so mused means thought, as a past tense verb.

clue.text: Animal falling over in hunger

indicators.note: falling over means the letters are toppled back to front
in means the letters are found inside the word hunger

explanation.surface: An animal collapses from starvation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives UNG from hUNGer; 'falling over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnu is a wildebeest, a large African antelope.
